title: A classmate reads it
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The mill-jacket classmate reads the digest at the long table. He reads it twice. He says the dog's not right. There is no dog. He means the gull.

panels.composition: The college cafeteria. The CLASSMATE in the mill jacket with the digest open, reading. WOOD across from him with corn.

image.prompt: an older man in a mill jacket reading a small stapled booklet at a cafeteria table while a young man eats across from him, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The classmate turning back to the front. Reading it again.

image.prompt: close on weathered hands turning a small photocopied booklet back to its first page, black and white, no words
an older man tapping the margin of a photocopied comic with a thick finger, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The margin gull, two strokes. The classmate's finger on it. Wood looking at it as a dog for the first time.

image.prompt: close on a tiny two-stroke bird mark in a comic's margin under a thick fingertip, black and white, no words
image.notes: The gull read as a dog, a month before the dog.

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'Dog's not right.' A month before the dog.
